data.method: exp(fitted log-yield slope × ONI) − 1, × production, at two ONI values the record contains; value at stake = tonnes × latest World Bank price. No world-price model, no probability weighting.
data.honesty: Conditional estimates from a linear fit without out-of-sample validation. CPC's OND 2026 RONI median (+2.67) is beyond the fitted range; figures at the record ONI are the largest the fit can support, not a ceiling on the event.

regions.label: Southern Africa · maize
regions.precedent: Niño3.4 explains 45–53% of seasonal rainfall variance (Funk et al. 2016). r≈−0.53/−0.56 for rainfall. 2015-16: regional maize ~7.2 Mt, 27% below the prior year and 38% below the 5-year average. 2023-24: Zimbabwe maize −72%, Zambia −54%, South Africa yield −17%. 2026 outlook: SADC’s SARCOF-33 statement from 28 Aug 2026 favours below-normal October–December rainfall across most of the region, but normal to above-normal rainfall in northern Zambia, central Malawi and northern Mozambique, with above-normal rainfall in the extreme north of Zambia and Malawi; the broad dry signal continues into January–March 2027.

regions.label: Horn of Africa · OND short rains
regions.precedent: Above-average short rains in only 12 of 20 El Niño events (1901–91). The El Niño signal here is wet, which means flood risk, not simply benefit. 2026 outlook: ICPAC’s 10 Sep 2026 summary for the GHACOF-74 October–December season gives a 90% chance of enhanced rainfall over southern Ethiopia, central to southern Somalia and north-eastern Kenya; that probability applies to this forecast zone, not the whole Horn.

regions.label: Australia · wheat and barley
regions.precedent: −20.8% national yield composite across El Niño years. Individual events: 1994 ~−50%, 2002-03 −58%, 2018-19 crop 23% below the 20-year average, 2023 −36%. 2026 outlook: ABARES’ September 2026 crop report, checked 22 Sep 2026, forecasts 61 Mt of winter crops in 2026–27, down 12% year on year but 16% above the ten-year average, including 29.9 Mt of wheat, down 17%; southern growing conditions are favourable while northern New South Wales and Queensland are poor, and the report does not attribute the national production change to El Niño.

regions.label: India · kharif rice and the summer monsoon
regions.precedent: Monsoon rainfall–Niño3.4 correlation r≈−0.6; drought severity −2.0σ in El Niño years vs −1.3σ otherwise. Base rate of a deficient monsoon in an El Niño year is reported anywhere between 45% and 70% and is genuinely disputed. 2026 outlook: IMD’s 17 Sep 2026 extended-range bulletin reports all-India rainfall 15% below the long-period average from 1 Jun to 16 Sep 2026 and expects El Niño to strengthen through the remaining monsoon season; this is a season-to-date assessment, not a final monsoon total or a crop-loss estimate.

regions.label: Indonesia · rice (planting delay)
regions.precedent: A 30-day onset delay produces −11% / −6.5% in the following Jan–Apr harvest; ~1.4 Mt lost per 1 °C of August SST anomaly. 2026 outlook: BMKG’s 17 Sep 2026 forecast for 18–24 Sep 2026 links very strong El Niño and the dry season to widespread dryness, reports more than 60 consecutive rainless days across much of southern Indonesia, and still forecasts local heavy rain; it gives no rice-loss estimate.

regions.label: Philippines · rice
regions.precedent: +1 °C Jul–Sep produces −3.7% irrigated and −13.7% rainfed rice. 2015-16 production −11%. 2026 outlook: PAGASA’s September 2026 agroclimatic outlook, carrying the El Niño advisory of 7 Sep 2026, expects below-normal rainfall in most of Northern Luzon, Zambales, Bataan, Davao del Sur, Davao Occidental and Sarangani, with near-normal rain elsewhere; it warns of dry spells and drought while allowing above-normal western rainfall during the southwest monsoon.

regions.label: Peru & Ecuador · fisheries and coastal flooding
regions.precedent: The least contested ENSO-economic link in this compiled set, the 1972 anchoveta collapse is documented in the fisheries and the economics literature alike. Anchoveta catch fell from 10.3 Mt (1971) to 4.4 Mt (1972); biomass fell from 5.8 Mt to 1.2 Mt in 1997-98; Peru cancelled the entire first 2023-24 season, with a tac of 1.09 Mt against a 4.4 Mt/yr non-event average, >$1.4 bn in lost export sales and about 0.5% of Peruvian GDP. Peru's 2023 coastal El Niño cut GDP growth by 1.1 pp. 2026 outlook: ENFEN N° 16-2026 of 14 Sep 2026 maintains the coastal El Niño alert, expects above-normal rain and river flows on Peru’s north coast mainly from November, and expects north-centre anchoveta to remain deeper and concentrated near shore. ERFEN 08-2026 of 4 Sep 2026 forecasts normal to above-normal September coastal rainfall in Ecuador and warns that elevated sea levels combined with high tides or waves can increase coastal flooding and erosion.
